buildings.description:
Publishes the human guide, browsable pattern library, package references, and
generated agent documentation used to apply JSKIT consistently.
buildings.name: guidance
buildings.publicContract:
Readers can browse the documentation site or consume the distributed agent-docs
package. Human guide sources define architectural meaning; the documented build
generates packaged references and pattern projections. Generated outputs must
remain reproducible from their authored sources.
buildings.title: Framework guidance and patterns

buildings.description:
Provides the capability, feature, action, HTTP, storage, realtime, and mobile
runtime primitives from which applications assemble their own behavior.
buildings.name: application-runtime
buildings.publicContract:
Applications import explicit npm entry points and compose named capabilities,
providers, actions, and runtime adapters. Long-running work and application
policy remain owned by the consuming application. Missing requirements fail at
composition or at the relevant operation boundary rather than being resolved
through a global service locator.
buildings.title: Application runtime composition

buildings.description:
Provides conversation runtimes, provider selection, voice support, reusable
connector account management, and focused third-party operations.
buildings.name: assistant-and-integrations
buildings.publicContract:
Applications select supported assistant and connector providers, retain their
own conversation and connection identities, and supply credentials through
server-side environment references. Conversations preserve provider lifecycle,
streaming, attachment, recovery, and storage contracts. Connector operations
remain scoped to the application and user or workspace that owns the account.

Transcript readers accept server-owned `pageUnit: "messages"` to count individual
user, assistant and system messages, excluding reasoning and commentary. The
default remains whole stored turns for internal consumers. The shared browser
page-size default is ten. Hosts select message pagination for browser reads.
History reads return an opaque `nextBeforeTurnId` cursor, including a message-role
boundary when a page splits a stored turn. Browser bindings follow that cursor
and merge partial turns without losing either half. Live patches retain whole
boundary turns and their progress rather than trimming by raw storage row count.
Pagination is a read-only projection; saved identities and records do not change.

Native conversations optionally report content-free delivery timings through
`onDeliveryTiming`. One shared observer supplies milestone names, monotonic
durations and message attribution for Codex, Claude and OpenCode; their original
native owners mark acknowledgement before receipt persistence. Observer work
does not block dispatch or alter saved conversation data.

Claude's native turn owner follows automatic task-notification continuations and
the complete live background-task inventory. Non-ambient native work keeps the
conversation active, including Bash and remote tasks; repeated status events do
not complete the same activity twice. Steering after the main loop has finished
does not wait for another interrupt result from that finished loop. The retained
host receives normalized continuation and diagnostic events without prompt or
response contents, and continues to own persistence and operator logging.
Older completion checkpoints cannot overwrite a newer native continuation.
Split native text keeps its live output identity until the API message identifies
it as tool commentary or an answer; restored history uses the same classification.
Renewal recovery joins the exact running turn or requires its saved completed
state before accepting history text. Accepted but unconfirmed input is never
submitted again automatically.
The execution receipt remains observed after initialization, so a parent exit
cannot be hidden by children retaining its output pipe. Concurrent cleanup calls
join one process stop and its interrupted-state checkpoint. Unconfirmed retained
cleanup exposes observation loss through the existing host status contract.
Closing a session cancels native startup before waiting for preparation to drain;
late configuration cannot launch a successor after Stop. Failed cleanup retains
its owner for an explicit retry rather than starting another hidden stop attempt.
Account queries deduplicate by account identity, and invalidation cancels held
startup and reads before awaiting their owned cleanup. Borrowed conversations
remain owned by their original lifecycle. Requests also retain the invalidation
revision across account lookup and retained cleanup: an older request cannot
launch a successor process or refill the cache after reconnection.

The retained browser goal binding distinguishes an unknown goal from a confirmed
empty goal. Initial and replacement reads display loading; failed reads hide
stale actions and report unavailability. Starting, pausing, resuming and cancelling
labels describe the actual command, not a background read or message admission.
Codex Pause combines native scheduling pause with the existing verified turn
interrupt, preserving the goal identity and budget for Resume. Cleanup failure
is reported rather than treating paused scheduling as proof that work stopped.

The native settings bridge authorizes configuration against the original scope
and uses its configured host and driver. Claude applies model and effort controls
to the retained process during a turn when its instructions and tool identity
are unchanged. Codex model and effort changes confirm the native settings
snapshot, including an already-applied selection that emits no change event.
Provider changes use the existing thread-control recovery owner: hold goal
scheduling, let the current turn finish, refresh credentials and reload the same
thread, then restore only the same unchanged goal. Later settings replace a
pending choice; user Pause, Cancel, replacement and closure prevent automatic
restoration. Failed deferred changes expose the native paused goal and emit a
settings failure diagnostic. Neither operation sends another user message or
clears a goal.

An OpenCode process acquired for helpers can exist before the main conversation
has a native ID. Stopping its idle main turn is a no-op; session closure still
drains owned helpers and releases the process without interrupting peer sessions.
An active turn with a missing native identity remains an error, never a
successful Stop.
buildings.title: Assistants and external integrations

buildings.description:
Provides reusable database, resource, CRUD, JSON API, upload, and transactional
payment or reward mechanics while leaving schemas and product workflows with
their owning package or application.
buildings.name: data-and-resources
buildings.publicContract:
Consumers select a supported database driver, discover package-owned immutable
migrations, and use explicit repositories and transactions. Resource operations
provide validated read and mutation contracts, predictable missing-record and
failure behavior, and application-supplied authorization context. Upload,
payment, and reward facilities require application-owned configuration and
storage; selecting a package does not provision an external service.
buildings.title: Data and resource operations

buildings.description:
Provides authentication-neutral identity contracts plus local and Supabase
providers, account profiles, authenticated web routes, and workspace tenancy.
buildings.name: identity-and-workspaces
buildings.publicContract:
Applications choose and configure an authentication provider, associate its
verified identity with existing application users, and authorize account and
workspace operations through explicit features and routes. Managed Preview can
exchange a host-authorized selector for an existing development user's normal
application session; it neither creates users nor grants roles.
buildings.title: Identity, users, and workspaces

buildings.description:
Provides Vue components, composables, shell placements, responsive resource
screens, authenticated account and workspace surfaces, billing, uploads, and
shared action feedback.
buildings.name: web-experiences
buildings.publicContract:
Applications compose public exports and placements into their own routes and
themes. Standard resource screens expose loading, empty, error, permission,
filtering, navigation, and mutation states through shared composables. The
application remains responsible for route policy, product vocabulary, and the
server authorization behind every visible action.
buildings.title: Web application experiences

buildings.description:
Coordinates workspace checks, generated documentation and catalogue artifacts,
and the versioned publication of all public JSKIT packages.
buildings.name: repository-lifecycle
buildings.publicContract:
`npm run verify` is the local aggregate check for lint, release contracts,
runtime dependency boundaries, CI declarations, package metadata, generated
artifacts, and workspace tests. Release preparation compares actual npm package
contents against each current exact published version. Matching packages retain
their versions; changed published packages receive one patch increment; suitable
unpublished versions are retained. All four local dependency fields and packaged
pattern/example manifests follow the final version map. Necessary consumer and
generated catalog/docs changes expand the release set until stable. The catalog's
self-version and complete release map are regenerated rather than normalized away.
Registry failures, newer stable published versions and occupied next versions
stop preparation before applying files.

Both preparation modes use an isolated source copy. Dry runs compute the same
selection without modifying checkout files or Git; real preparation applies
changed files and updates the lockfile through the existing package-lock-only
command only when its entries need refreshing. A failed lockfile refresh can be
retried through preparation without another version bump. Matching source and
lockfile are a no-op, and repeated preparation does not bump already unpublished
versions. Installed development dependencies and registry
access are required. Metadata, verified published contents and unchanged packs
are reused only within that invocation. All packing is sequential.

Publication accepts
only a clean, current `main` checkout and rechecks for newer stable registry
releases. It packs and checks every exact version
against npm before uploading any package, skips matching releases, rejects
different contents under an existing version, and fails on registry errors.
Hashes are compared first; a different hash triggers comparison of verified
archive files, links and permissions while ignoring tar timestamps and
compression. Absent versions upload those same candidate tarballs in dependency
order. A retry checks npm again and needs no release-resume state. Dry runs
perform the same registry preflight without uploading. Registry verification is
a separate network-dependent operation. `release` keeps its existing meaning:
verify and publish source prepared and committed through the separate command.
buildings.title: Repository verification and release

buildings.description:
Provides the published JSKIT package catalogue, package-graph validation,
shared ESLint presets, and workspace test helpers.
buildings.name: catalogue
buildings.publicContract:
The `jskit` executable checks or updates an application's coordinated JSKIT
package graph using published catalogue metadata. Repository validation checks
package metadata and dependency rules. Shared lint and test exports give JSKIT
packages and consumers consistent development conventions without generating
application source.

Hosts may supply additional manifests for separately composed packages without
changing npm workspace membership. Updates preserve host-owned npm scripts.
The CLI checks installed packages against root lockfiles; shared tooling also
checks the actual composed runtime graph through Node's real-path resolution,
including equal-version duplicate singleton runtimes. Catalog selection belongs
to the caller; checks never fetch a newer catalog.

The programmatic checks accept an explicit `sourcePackages` name-to-directory
map for development composition. Source preflight skips published declaration,
lock and installed-version comparisons only for these replaced names. The
composed graph validates every selected source manifest, follows required edges,
requires resolution to its exact real path and retains singleton checks even at
equal versions. Hosts must supply the materialized map to the composed check and
retain their external dependency and export validation. No CLI or updater flag
weakens published checks, and these checks never modify manifests or locks.
buildings.title: Package catalogue and development tooling

districts.description:
Owns the published JSKIT libraries, application patterns, package migrations,
browser-facing components, server runtimes, and the human and distributed agent
documentation. Packages expose explicit npm entry points so applications can
compose only the capabilities they need.
districts.title: Framework packages

districts.description:
Owns the package catalogue, package-graph checks, shared lint configuration,
and test helpers used to develop and release the workspace.
districts.title: Developer tooling

districts.description:
Owns workspace-level verification, generated-artifact checks, coordinated npm
release preparation and publication, and continuous-integration orchestration.
The more specific package and tooling directories retain ownership of their own
implementation.
districts.title: Repository operations
